material_symbols.terms_note: The visitor's browser contacts Google's servers to load the icons, and the observatory's About tab lists Google Fonts among the servers that can see a visitor's IP address.

prtc_regions.name: Puerto Rico Tourism Company — tourism regions

short.es: regiones de la Compañía de Turismo

prtc_regions.credit: Source: Puerto Rico Tourism Company, tourism regions (tourism.pr.gov/regions)
prtc_regions.access: FPR read the region lists on the PRTC page and typed each municipality's region into the observatory by hand. The observatory does not call tourism.pr.gov.
prtc_regions.cadence: The observatory's copy changes only when FPR updates it by hand. On 3 October 2026 the seven region lists on the PRTC page matched the observatory's list for all 78 municipalities.
prtc_regions.used_for: The tourism region of each municipality (municipalities.json and municipios.geojson), used to group figures by region.
prtc_regions.terms_note: The PRTC site footer reads '© 2026 - Puerto Rico Tourism Company. All rights reserved.' A tourism region is a Tourism Company grouping, not a Census, planning or political unit. Only the region names and which municipalities belong to each are used. If the Tourism Company changes its regions, the observatory stays out of date until FPR updates its list.

noaa_slr_scenarios.name: NOAA — Sea level rise scenarios (2022 report)
noaa_slr_scenarios.publisher: NOAA National Ocean Service, with partner agencies

short.es: escenarios de aumento del nivel del mar de NOAA (2022)

noaa_slr_scenarios.credit: Adapted from: Sweet, W.V., et al., 2022: Global and Regional Sea Level Rise Scenarios for the United States. NOAA Technical Report NOS 01. Values approximated by Foundation for Puerto Rico
noaa_slr_scenarios.access: No file is downloaded. FPR typed approximate values into the 3D map. They give global mean sea level in metres above the year-2000 level for four scenarios (Intermediate-Low, Intermediate, Intermediate-High and High) at 2020, 2050, 2100 and 2150. Values between those years are interpolated in a straight line.
noaa_slr_scenarios.cadence: NOAA issued the report in 2022, its first update since 2017. The observatory's numbers change only when FPR updates them by hand.
noaa_slr_scenarios.used_for: The Years clock on the 3D map: a year and a scenario give a rise in feet, which picks the nearest layer (1 to 10 feet) from NOAA's Sea Level Rise Viewer.
noaa_slr_scenarios.terms_note: The values are approximations of the report's global mean sea level tables. The 2100 values match the report, but some others differ: the 2050 Intermediate-Low value (0.24 m) is the report's observation-based extrapolation, not the scenario (0.20 m); the 2050 Intermediate (0.30 m) and High (0.44 m) values are 0.02 m and 0.01 m above the report (0.28 m and 0.43 m); the 2020 Intermediate-High and High values (0.07 m) are 0.01 m below the report (0.08 m); and the 2150 Intermediate-High and High values (2.9 m and 3.9 m) are 0.2 m above the report (2.7 m and 3.7 m). The values are global averages, not values for Puerto Rico's coast. The result is indicative, not a forecast. The report defines five scenarios (Low to High) and the observatory offers four, without Low. The report's notice says that use of its information for publicity or advertising of proprietary products or their tests is not authorized. Checked again on 2026-10-19 for the Data management page: the report states no license and no public-domain notice, and its notice restricts one use (publicity or advertising of proprietary products), so the class stays unstated.

github_pages.name: GitHub Pages and Actions (hosting, nightly refresh)
github_pages.licence: Service terms, not a data license
github_pages.access: A workflow (GitHub Actions) publishes the site folder to GitHub Pages each time the site files change on the main branch and after each nightly refresh that changes data. A second workflow runs every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and refreshes the transit data. The chat's data-request button opens a GitHub new-issue page that the visitor must review and submit.
github_pages.cadence: Republished when the site files change and after each nightly refresh that changes data.
github_pages.used_for: Serving every page and data file of the observatory, running the nightly transit refresh, and the optional GitHub issue link in the chat.
github_pages.terms_note: This is a hosting service, not a data license. GitHub's Pages limits page says published sites may be no larger than 1 GB, with soft limits of 100 GB of bandwidth a month and 10 builds an hour (the build limit does not apply to custom workflows). Like any web host, GitHub receives the visitor's IP address when a page loads; see GitHub's privacy statement.

live_transit_checks.name: Real-time transit checks (ATI page, app listings)
live_transit_checks.publisher: Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI); app listings by their publishers; checks by FPR

more_links.label: transPRte on the Apple App Store

live_transit_checks.licence: Links and short factual statements only; no data copied
live_transit_checks.credit: Source: Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) review of public pages (the ATI open-data page, Google Play and the Apple App Store), 2 October 2026
live_transit_checks.access: FPR checked these pages by hand and recorded the results in operators.json, under the key 'live'. The observatory does not call these pages.
live_transit_checks.cadence: Checked once, on 2 October 2026. Nothing re-checks them automatically.
live_transit_checks.used_for: The 'what is live' table in the Transit tab, which says that real-time bus positions are not available to the public.
live_transit_checks.terms_note: On 3 October 2026 FPR opened three pages. The transPRte listing is published by SENDA Limited Liability Company, which says the app is independent and not affiliated with ATI, AMA or any agency; its release notes say it shows ATI express buses T3, E10, E20, E30, E40, C22, C35 and C36 'using the positions the operator publishes'. The AMA Móvil listing on Google Play is published under the Government of Puerto Rico and lists real-time bus tracking among its features; it does not say whether a public data feed exists. ATI's urban transportation page points riders to the City Experiences app to monitor ferry service in real time. The aircraft (ADS-B) row in the table names no web address, and the observatory calls no ADS-B service. Each page keeps its publisher's terms.

fpr_twin.name: PR Data Observatory build records (FPR)
fpr_twin.credit: Source: Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory, Snapshot 2026-10
fpr_twin.access: Written by the programs that build the observatory's data and published as meta.json, registry.json and wanted.json. FPR edits wanted.json by hand. Nothing is downloaded from another party.
fpr_twin.cadence: meta.json and registry.json are rewritten each time FPR rebuilds the data (a new snapshot). wanted.json changes only when FPR edits it (last updated 3 October 2026).
fpr_twin.used_for: The snapshot label, dates and counts (meta.json); each published file's size and its share of the 1 GB GitHub Pages limit (registry.json); and the list of candidate datasets that the chat reads to answer what is missing (wanted.json: 30 candidates in the 2026-10 snapshot).
fpr_twin.terms_note: wanted.json lists candidate datasets only. Their licenses have not been confirmed, and the list is not a source of data in the observatory.

jp_comunidades_especiales.name: Junta de Planificación — Delimitation of the Comunidades Especiales (2006)
jp_comunidades_especiales.publisher: Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico (Government of Puerto Rico)

more_links.label: Another public copy of the same layer (named delim_comunidades_especiales_2006)

short.es: delimitación de Comunidades Especiales (Junta de Planificación)

jp_comunidades_especiales.credit: Source: Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico, delimitation of the Comunidades Especiales (Ley 1-2001), 2006
jp_comunidades_especiales.access: The build reads a public copy of the Junta's layer on ArcGIS Online (services6.arcgis.com, Comunidades_Especiales, layer 0), held by the same account as the copy of the Land Use Plan the observatory uses. It shows no description, owner organisation or license text. A second public copy with the same 713 polygons and fields is named delim_comunidades_especiales_2006. The Junta's own map service (MIPR, Comunidades) did not answer on 2026-10-06.
jp_comunidades_especiales.cadence: A 2006 delimitation. The observatory downloads it once and does not refresh it unless the build is run with its refresh option.
jp_comunidades_especiales.used_for: The Comunidades Especiales outlines on the 2D map (comunidades.geojson) and the name, place, housing units, community type and reported hazards shown when you click one.
jp_comunidades_especiales.terms_note: The layer comes with no license text. Ley 1-2001 created the Comunidades Especiales program; communities designated after this delimitation may be missing. The attributes come from a community inventory taken with the delimitation and describe conditions at that time.

fpr_wcrp.name: FPR — Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program, list of communities
fpr_wcrp.credit: Source: Foundation for Puerto Rico, Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program, list of communities and program tracker as of 2026-10-06
fpr_wcrp.access: FPR's WCRP document index (WCRP-RAG, list_comunidades) lists each community with its municipality, WCRP region, plan status and subrecipient; FPR copied that list into wcrp_comunidades.csv on 2026-10-06. Seven communities in phase 1 have no documents in that index yet, so their rows come from FPR's Smartsheet tracker of the program (TRACKER_Planning Phases, 79 communities) and their municipality from their work plans. Both sources are internal; the observatory publishes seven columns (community, plan status, municipality, the place the point was set from, region, subrecipient and how the point was placed) and an approximate point.
fpr_wcrp.cadence: Copied once, on 2026-10-06. Nothing refreshes it automatically: FPR adds or updates rows in the CSV by hand and runs wcrp.py.
fpr_wcrp.used_for: The WCRP communities points on the 2D map (wcrp.geojson): name, municipality, region, plan status, subrecipient, the place the point was set from and how the approximate point was placed.
fpr_wcrp.terms_note: The community plans define each community's area only in a PDF map, so the observatory places one approximate point per community and does not draw the plan's boundary. Foundation for Puerto Rico runs WCRP in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH), with HUD CDBG-DR funds.

wcrp_rvi.name: Hunter College for Foundation for Puerto Rico — WCRP Risk and Vulnerability Indicators (RVI), 2022
wcrp_rvi.publisher: Hunter College (City University of New York) for Foundation for Puerto Rico, Whole Community Resilience Planning program; published on ArcGIS Online by the PlanningCDBG account
wcrp_rvi.licence: No open license stated: the services' licenseInfo and accessInformation fields are empty. FPR publishes the data on the observatory with the program's approval (confirmed on 2026-10-19); others should ask PRDOH and FPR before re-using them

short.es: Indicadores de Riesgo y Vulnerabilidad de WCRP (2022)

wcrp_rvi.credit: Source: Hunter College for Foundation for Puerto Rico, Risk and Vulnerability Indicators (RVI), Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program, 2022; ACS 2015-2019 and other inputs
wcrp_rvi.access: wcrp_rvi.py reads the public ArcGIS REST services with no key: All_Indicator (the OVERALL row of each of the 901 barrios carries the six area indices, the overall index and their ranks) and Master_Data_Table_Update (the barrio input values of each indicator; the municipio and Puerto Rico columns are not kept). It also reads each service's ArcGIS Online item to record the license fields and the date of the last data edit (March 2022). The method is described in the RVI white paper (Hunter College, December 2021), an internal FPR document.
wcrp_rvi.cadence: Published once (data last edited 15-21 March 2022). python wcrp_rvi.py --refresh reads the services again; a later edit would show in the file's versions.orig.services.
wcrp_rvi.used_for: The original 2022 vulnerability index and ranks by barrio (wcrp_rvi_barrio.json, keys rvi_*_orig), the input values shown in the WCRP page's pop-up (wcrp_rvi_inputs.json, fields o_*), and the checks of the observatory's rebuild against the original.
wcrp_rvi.terms_note: Foundation for Puerto Rico runs WCRP in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH), with HUD CDBG-DR funds (U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development). The services carry no license or access terms, the item descriptions are empty and the only tag is 'Vivienda', so no open license is stated. FPR approved publication on 2026-10-19 and confirmed the same day that its approval covers republishing this source on the observatory. That approval is not an open license: anyone else who wants to re-use the data should ask PRDOH and FPR first. The WCRP page carries an 'In review' marker and may change.

ppr_type1.name: Policía de Puerto Rico — Delitos Tipo I (Type I crimes), published by the Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico
ppr_type1.publisher: Policía de Puerto Rico, División de Estadísticas de la Criminalidad; published by the Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico
ppr_type1.licence: No license stated (official statistics of the Government of Puerto Rico)

short.en: Puerto Rico Police Type I crimes
short.es: delitos Tipo I de la Policía de Puerto Rico

ppr_type1.credit: Source: Policía de Puerto Rico, División de Estadísticas de la Criminalidad, Delitos Tipo I por municipio (December reports), published by the Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico
ppr_type1.access: One file per year, no key: the December report, which counts January to December. 2017 to 2022 are Excel files (.xls, sheet MUNICIPIO or MUNICIPIOS); 2023 on are ZIP files of PDFs, of which the build reads the municipality table with pdftotext. The 2017 to 2024 files are on the old Instituto site, whose certificate chain is incomplete (Python rejects it; the build falls back to curl). Later files are found on the product page of the new site.
ppr_type1.cadence: Monthly year-to-date reports; the observatory uses only the December report of each year. In the 2026-10 snapshot it holds 2017 to 2025. A new year needs `python economy_series.py --police --refresh` after the Instituto posts the December report (January or February).
ppr_type1.used_for: Type I crimes, violent and property crimes and murders by municipality and calendar year (economy_series.json, keys crime_type1, crime_violent, crime_property, crime_murders).
ppr_type1.terms_note: The pages state no license or reuse terms. The reports carry the name or e-mail of the Police staff who prepared them (in page footers and file properties); the build reads only the counts and publishes no names. Counts are complaints (querellas) recorded by the Police, not all crimes committed. The Police's public crime map (incidenciacriminal.policia.pr.gov) is a different product: it shows single incidents with addresses and is not used.

nhc_slosh.name: NHC — SLOSH storm surge maps for Puerto Rico (Maximum of MEOWs, category 1 to 5, high tide)
nhc_slosh.publisher: NOAA National Hurricane Center (NHC), Storm Surge Unit

more_links.label: Puerto Rico maps the observatory reads (PR_SLOSH_MOM_Inundation.zip, 7.3 MB)
About SLOSH and the MOM product

nhc_slosh.credit: Source: NOAA National Hurricane Center, SLOSH Maximum of MEOWs storm surge maps for Puerto Rico (2018)
nhc_slosh.access: One public ZIP file, no key: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/hazardmaps/PR_SLOSH_MOM_Inundation.zip (7.3 MB, dated 30 November 2018). It holds five GeoTIFFs, one per hurricane category, of about 10 m cells in NAD83, each cell coded by the depth of water above ground in 1 ft bands (1 = under 1 ft, 2 = 1 to 2 ft, and so on). exposure.py downloads it once, reads the cell under each 2020 Census block's internal point with the project's own GeoTIFF reader (raster.py), and keeps only the counts of residents and housing units of each area, not the maps.
nhc_slosh.cadence: NHC published the Puerto Rico maps in November 2018 (the files inside are dated November 2017) and has not replaced them since; the mainland maps were updated later (version 4). The freshness check watches the ZIP file's date and size. A new file is used only when FPR rebuilds the exposure series with the refresh option.
nhc_slosh.used_for: The residents and housing units in the area that NOAA's storm surge maps show flooded by a category 1 to 5 hurricane, at any depth and under 3 ft of water or more, by municipio, barrio and census tract (exposure_municipio.json, exposure_barrio.json, exposure_tract.json; families surge_cat1 to surge_cat5 and surge_deep_cat1 to surge_deep_cat5).
nhc_slosh.terms_note: NHC says information on government servers may be used freely and is in the public domain, and that it must not be modified and then presented as official government material. The map metadata say the data show the scale of potential flooding, not the exact location, for general awareness of the storm surge hazard at a city or community level, not for a parcel or grid cell; they do not account for erosion, subsidence or future construction, and the risk may extend beyond the SLOSH model's grids. They are a planning reference and storm surge awareness tool, not for navigation, permitting, legal or regulatory purposes. Each map is the Maximum of MEOWs (MOM): for each category, the highest water among many hypothetical storms of different tracks, speeds and sizes, at high tide, so it is a near worst case, not one storm. The maps are not evacuation zones; those are set by Puerto Rico's emergency management bureau.

nces_ipeds.name: NCES — IPEDS completions and institutional directory
nces_ipeds.publisher: National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), US Department of Education

more_links.label: IPEDS completions survey, about the data

nces_ipeds.credit: Source: NCES, Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), completions and directory
nces_ipeds.access: Two ZIP files a year from NCES's IPEDS Data Center, no key: https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/data/C{year}_A.zip (completions: awards by institution, six-digit CIP field, award level and first or second major) and HD{year}.zip (the directory: each institution's state and county). The revised file inside a ZIP (_RV) is read when NCES has published one. degrees.py keeps only the counts of each municipio.
nces_ipeds.cadence: NCES publishes a year's completions about a year after it ends, and revises it the next year. The observatory holds academic years ending 2015 to 2024. The freshness check looks for the next year's file every 30 days; when it appears, raise LAST in degrees.py and rebuild.
nces_ipeds.used_for: Degrees and certificates awarded by level and broad field, by municipio of the campus, academic years ending 2015 to 2024 (degrees_series.json).
nces_ipeds.terms_note: IPEDS data are a US Government work and in the public domain. Institutions report their own counts; NCES imputes for a few that do not report. Counts follow the campus, not where graduates live; a student with two majors is counted once here (first majors).

urban_crdc.name: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal: Civil Rights Data Collection
urban_crdc.publisher: US Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights, via the Urban Institute

more_links.label: Civil Rights Data Collection (Office for Civil Rights)

urban_crdc.licence: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0) for the portal, which asks to credit the Urban Institute and the original source; the NCES data are US federal (public domain)
urban_crdc.credit: Source: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal, Civil Rights Data Collection, US Department of Education Office for Civil Rights
urban_crdc.access: The Urban Institute's Education Data Portal API, no key, Puerto Rico's all-students rows only: schools/crdc/enrollment/{year}/race/sex, schools/crdc/chronic-absenteeism/{year}/race/sex and schools/crdc/teachers-staff/{year}, with fips=72 and race, sex, disability, English learner and homeless set to 99 (total). school_conditions.py keeps the counts of each school only in its cache and publishes municipio totals.
urban_crdc.cadence: The Civil Rights Data Collection runs every two years; 2019-20 was not collected (the pandemic). The observatory holds 2017-18 and 2021-22; 2023-24 is the next. The portal was slow on 2026-11-18 (requests timed out); the script tries each page up to six times.
urban_crdc.used_for: Chronic absence, students per counselor, schools with a nurse and schools with no counselor, by municipio, school years 2017-18 and 2021-22 (school_conditions_series.json).
urban_crdc.terms_note: The portal is under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0) and asks to credit the Urban Institute and the original source; the CRDC is a US Government work. Schools report their own figures to the Office for Civil Rights; the office does not audit them, and how a school counts an absence can differ.

urban_edfacts.name: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal: EDFacts state assessments
urban_edfacts.publisher: US Department of Education (EDFacts), via the Urban Institute

more_links.label: Instituto de Estadísticas: proficiency in META-PR (island, 2018-19)

urban_edfacts.licence: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0) for the portal, which asks to credit the Urban Institute and the original source; the NCES data are US federal (public domain)
urban_edfacts.credit: Source: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal, EDFacts state assessments, US Department of Education
urban_edfacts.access: The Urban Institute's Education Data Portal API, no key: schools/edfacts/assessments/{year}/grade-99 with fips=72 and every subgroup set to 99 (all students). proficiency.py keeps each school's students tested and share proficient only in its cache and publishes municipio shares.
urban_edfacts.cadence: The portal holds Puerto Rico's school results for 2009-10 to 2018-19; 2019-20 was not tested, and later years are not there. ED Data Express answers a script with an empty page and the Department of Education's school profile is a Power BI report, so 2018-19 is the newest result by school a script can read (checked 2026-11-18). The island figures for later years appear in the press and in the Department's reports, not by municipio.
urban_edfacts.used_for: Students proficient in reading (Spanish) and math, by municipio, school years 2014-15 to 2018-19 (proficiency_series.json).
urban_edfacts.terms_note: The portal is under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0) and asks to credit the Urban Institute and the original source; EDFacts is a US Government work. To protect students, a small school's share comes as a range; the observatory uses its middle and keeps the island's lowest and highest possible figures in the notes.

cms_nppes.name: CMS — National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES), monthly full file
cms_nppes.credit: Source: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES)
cms_nppes.access: The monthly full replacement file from https://download.cms.gov/nppes/NPI_Files.html (about 1.1 GB zipped, 11.8 GB unzipped), no key. providers.py reads the national CSV inside the ZIP as a stream and keeps, for Puerto Rico's individual providers only, the primary taxonomy code, practice city and ZIP code, last update year and whether the NPI is active: no name, NPI, address or telephone reaches the cache.
cms_nppes.cadence: CMS publishes a new full file each month. The observatory holds NPPES_November_2026_V2.zip; python providers.py --refresh downloads the newest.
cms_nppes.used_for: Health care providers by type (physicians, psychiatrists, dentists, nurse practitioners and physician assistants, psychologists, counselors and social workers, pharmacists), by municipio (providers_series.json).
cms_nppes.terms_note: NPPES data are a US Government work and public by law (45 CFR 162.410 lets CMS disclose them). The rows name individual providers: the observatory keeps none of that and publishes counts by municipio only, with no count from 1 to 9. Providers register and update their own records; many never update a record, so a listing does not prove a provider still practises.

urban_ccd.name: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal: NCES Common Core of Data school directory
urban_ccd.publisher: Urban Institute (Education Data Portal), republishing the US Department of Education's National Center for Education Statistics (NCES)
urban_ccd.licence: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0) for the portal, which asks to credit the Urban Institute and the original source; the NCES data are US federal (public domain)
urban_ccd.cadence: NCES publishes each school year about two years after it starts; the portal adds it after. The observatory renews the series when FPR rebuilds the data (python education_series.py).
urban_ccd.credit: Source: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal, Common Core of Data school directory, National Center for Education Statistics; downloaded October 2026
urban_ccd.access: The portal's public API (no key), one request per school year for Puerto Rico (fips=72). The build keeps ten columns (school id, year, county, status, type, level, students, teachers, charter, virtual) and drops names, addresses, telephone numbers and coordinates before anything is written to disk.
urban_ccd.used_for: Public schools open, students, teachers, students per teacher and closures in each municipality, every school year since 2010 (education_series.json: sch_open, sch_enroll, sch_teachers, sch_ptr, sch_closed).

urban_ipeds.name: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal: NCES IPEDS directory and fall enrollment
urban_ipeds.publisher: Urban Institute (Education Data Portal), republishing the US Department of Education's National Center for Education Statistics (NCES)
urban_ipeds.licence: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0) for the portal, which asks to credit the Urban Institute and the original source; the NCES data are US federal (public domain)
urban_ipeds.cadence: NCES publishes each school year about two years after it starts; the portal adds it after. The observatory renews the series when FPR rebuilds the data (python education_series.py).
urban_ipeds.credit: Source: Urban Institute, Education Data Portal, Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) directory and fall enrollment, National Center for Education Statistics; downloaded October 2026
urban_ipeds.access: The portal's public API (no key): the directory and the undergraduate and graduate fall enrollment totals for Puerto Rico (fips=72), one request each per year. The build keeps the institution id, county, sector and enrollment and drops names, addresses, telephone numbers, web addresses and officers' names before anything is written to disk.
urban_ipeds.used_for: Postsecondary institutions and their fall enrollment in each municipality (education_series.json: he_inst, he_enroll).

cms_provider_data.name: CMS — Provider Data Catalog (hospitals, dialysis facilities, nursing homes, home health agencies, hospice)

eia_860m.name: EIA — Form EIA-860M, Monthly Update to the Annual Electric Generator Report
eia_860m.credit: Source: US Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-860M, generators of Puerto Rico
eia_860m.access: The monthly Excel file (no key), sheets Operating_PR and Planned_PR. infrastructure_series.py keeps the plant id, technology, nameplate capacity, status and point of each operating generator for the counts by municipality; power_plants.py keeps those and the plant name, battery energy, operating year and planned month for the Power plants layer. Owner names are never kept.
eia_860m.cadence: EIA publishes a month about seven weeks after it ends. The refresh bot reads the newest file each month (python infrastructure_series.py --refresh; python power_plants.py --refresh).
eia_860m.used_for: The Power plants map layer (power_plants.geojson), and the operating power plants, generating capacity and renewable capacity of each municipality (infrastructure_series.json: power_*).

fhwa_nbi.name: FHWA — National Bridge Inventory
fhwa_nbi.credit: Source: US Federal Highway Administration, National Bridge Inventory, Puerto Rico delimited files 2016-2025
fhwa_nbi.access: The yearly delimited file of Puerto Rico (no key). infrastructure_series.py keeps the county code and the condition ratings for the counts by municipio; transport_inventories.py keeps, for the newest year, each bridge's structure number, point, road carried, feature crossed, condition, lowest rating, year built and rebuilt, daily traffic and its year, trucks, detour, length, status, scour code, last inspection and owner code.
fhwa_nbi.cadence: FHWA publishes each year's inventory in the following spring; the format changes to the Specifications for the National Bridge Inventory (SNBI) from 2026 on.
fhwa_nbi.used_for: Highway bridges and bridges in poor condition in each municipality, every year (bridges_series.json), and the Bridges and tunnels map layer (bridges.geojson). Also the bridges that close (poor condition or closed) and those that stay open (good or fair) in the estimate of residents cut off from hospitals (cutoff_series.json, cutoff_barrio.json).

fhwa_hpms.name: FHWA — Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS)
fhwa_hpms.publisher: US Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), Office of Highway Policy Information; layer served by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) in the National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD)

more_links.label: HPMS_FULL_PR_2025 on geo.dot.gov (ArcGIS REST, the layer the build reads)
HPMS Field Manual (definitions of AADT, functional class, IRI)
23 CFR 490.313: IRI thresholds for pavement condition (good, fair, poor)
HPMS Field Manual, item 26: K_Factor (design-hour volume)

fhwa_hpms.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. § 105), available for unrestricted public use

short.es: HPMS de la FHWA

fhwa_hpms.credit: Source: US Department of Transportation, Federal Highway Administration, Office of Highway Policy Information, Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS), Puerto Rico, data year 2025 (traffic) and 2024 (route analysis)
fhwa_hpms.access: Two reads, no key. (1) traffic.py: FHWA's HPMS_FULL_PR_<year> feature service on geo.dot.gov, newest data year (2025: 262,462 road sections, about 160 requests), cached in cache/traffic/; it publishes the main roads with a count (traffic_roads.geojson) and municipio figures (traffic_series.json). (2) The road-features analysis of the Route analysis (road_flow.py, kept with that work): the BTS layer HPMS_National_Current, 2024 data, cached on a local computer; only counts of junctions reach site/data.
fhwa_hpms.cadence: Puerto Rico, through the DTOP, reports to FHWA every year; FHWA publishes a data year the year after (2025 in 2026). The list of services on geo.dot.gov is checked every 30 days; a new year is rebuilt with traffic.py --refresh after a person looks at it. The Route analysis keeps its 2024 snapshot until it is redone.
fhwa_hpms.used_for: The map layer Traffic on the main roads and, for each municipio, daily vehicle-kilometres, per resident, km of arterials and major collectors, the busiest count, the truck share and the share of measured main roads with rough pavement (traffic.py); the traffic on the roads each simulated connection between municipios follows (transit_links.py); and the estimated design-hour volume at each signalised junction and roundabout in the Route analysis (route_compare.json).
fhwa_hpms.terms_note: HPMS reports state and federal-aid roads, not most local streets, so a junction with no HPMS road nearby has no flow. K is required only on Sample Panel sections, and the Field Manual says statewide or system-wide values shall not be used. For 764 of the 1,582 junctions (48%) the road has no K and the observatory used the median K of its functional class (k_imputed): the observatory's own estimate, which HPMS guidance does not endorse. AADT is an annual average of both directions; AADT x K is a design-hour volume (one of the busiest hours of the year), not a typical weekday peak, and says nothing about speed or delay. The NTAD item advises against comparing states on the sampled items; only Puerto Rico is used.

fema_nri.name: FEMA — National Risk Index, county table

more_links.label: County table service (FEMA's ArcGIS Online, for developers)

fema_nri.credit: Source: FEMA, National Risk Index (December 2025), county table for Puerto Rico
fema_nri.access: FEMA's own ArcGIS Online service for the county table (no key); the download page refuses scripts. The build reads the expected annual loss in all and for six hazards, and checks that the composite risk score, social vulnerability and community resilience are still empty for Puerto Rico.
fema_nri.cadence: FEMA releases a new version every year or two. The observatory renews it when FPR rebuilds the data (python environment_series.py).
fema_nri.used_for: Expected annual loss from natural hazards in each municipio, in all and for hurricane wind, earthquake, inland flooding, landslide, coastal flooding and tsunami (environment_series.json: nri_eal_*).

census_cre.name: Census Bureau — Community Resilience Estimates for Puerto Rico

more_links.label: Files (Puerto Rico in each year's pr folder)

census_cre.licence: US federal government data (public domain); cite the Census Bureau as the source
census_cre.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, Community Resilience Estimates for Puerto Rico, 2019-2024
census_cre.access: The Puerto Rico files of each release (no key): the municipio file and the island row of the tract file. The build keeps the three shares of residents by number of risk factors and their margins of error.
census_cre.cadence: A release every year since 2021 (and 2019). The observatory adds a new one when FPR rebuilds the data.
census_cre.used_for: Residents with no, one or two, and three or more risk factors, with margins (hazard_series.json: cre_*).

usgs_slope_failures.name: USGS — Map of slope-failure locations in Puerto Rico after Hurricane María (Hughes and others, 2019)
usgs_slope_failures.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS), with the University of Puerto Rico at Mayagüez

more_links.label: Copy kept by the first author at UPRM (the source the build reads)

usgs_slope_failures.credit: Source: Hughes, K.S., Bayouth García, D., Martínez Milian, G.O., Schulz, W.H., and Baum, R.L., 2019, Map of slope-failure locations in Puerto Rico after Hurricane María: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P9BVMD74
usgs_slope_failures.access: The USGS catalogue (ScienceBase) refuses scripts, so the build reads the copy the data release's first author keeps on ArcGIS Online at UPRM (no key): only each point's location. The copy's municipio and barrio fields are not used; each point is placed by the municipal boundary.
usgs_slope_failures.used_for: Landslides mapped after Hurricane María in each municipio, in all and per km² of land (environment_series.json: landslides_*).

usgs_landslide_map.name: USGS — Landslide susceptibility map of Puerto Rico (Hughes and Schulz, 2020)
usgs_landslide_map.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS), with the University of Puerto Rico at Mayagüez

more_links.label: The report: Open-File Report 2020-1022 (method, table 5, limits)
Tile copy kept by the first author at UPRM (the source the build reads)

usgs_landslide_map.licence: US federal government data (public domain); the data release states CC0 1.0
usgs_landslide_map.credit: Source: Hughes, K.S., and Schulz, W.H., 2020, Map depicting susceptibility to landslides triggered by intense rainfall, Puerto Rico: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 2020-1022, https://doi.org/10.3133/ofr20201022; Schulz, W.H., and Hughes, K.S., 2021, Geographic information system layer of a map depicting susceptibility to landslides triggered by intense rainfall, Puerto Rico: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P990ZP4C
usgs_landslide_map.access: The data release (a 5 m GeoTIFF of the main island in five classes) is on ScienceBase, which refuses scripted downloads behind a bot check; the observatory does not get around it. The build reads the copy the first author keeps on ArcGIS Online at UPRM (no key): the PNG map tiles of zoom 15 (about 4.5 m a pixel on the ground), one flat colour per class, decoded back into the classes. Two checks against the report prove they are the published map: the area of each class is the report's share of the island (40, 30, 20, 9 and 1%) and the 71,431 slope failures of Hurricane María fall in the classes as the report's table 5 says. Only areas and counts are kept; no tile or raster is published.
usgs_landslide_map.cadence: Static: one model (2020; GIS layer 2022). The build checks the copy's last edit date on ArcGIS Online.
usgs_landslide_map.used_for: The share of the land in the high, very high and extremely high classes, and the 2020 residents living there, for each barrio and municipio (landslide_series.json, landslide_barrio.json). The Landslide susceptibility layer of the 2D map, drawn from the same tile copy while the layer is on (nothing is stored).
usgs_landslide_map.terms_note: USGS-authored data are in the public domain in the United States; the USGS data release page states CC0 1.0. The authors say the map is for planning and emergency preparation and is not a substitute for a site-specific slope-stability study by licensed geologists and engineers; it does not show where a landslide travels downhill, and deep bedrock landslides and earthquake-triggered ones are poorly represented.

usda_ssurgo.name: USDA NRCS — Soil Survey Geographic Database (SSURGO), Puerto Rico
usda_ssurgo.publisher: US Department of Agriculture, Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS)

more_links.label: Soil Data Access: the query service the build reads (for developers)
Web Soil Survey: the same data on NRCS's own map

short.es: estudio de suelos del NRCS (SSURGO)

usda_ssurgo.credit: Source: Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO) Database for Puerto Rico. Soils: USDA NRCS, SSURGO
usda_ssurgo.access: Keyless SQL queries to Soil Data Access (https://sdmdataaccess.sc.egov.usda.gov/Tabular/post.rest) for Puerto Rico's seven survey areas (PR682, PR684, PR686, PR688, PR689, PR700, PR787): the map unit polygons, their components, horizons, parent material, monthly flooding, farmland class and the NRCS rating for dwellings without basements. soils.py caches the answers in cache/soils/.
usda_ssurgo.cadence: NRCS refreshes SSURGO once a year (usually in October). The observatory reads it again only when soils.py runs with --refresh.
usda_ssurgo.used_for: The Soils layer of the 2D map (soils.geojson): the soil type and origin, the slope, the chemistry of the top 30 cm and three plain questions (flooding, farming, building houses) for each soil map unit.
usda_ssurgo.terms_note: USDA data are in the public domain in the United States; NRCS asks that the data be credited. NRCS says the maps are made for planning at the scale of the survey and are not a substitute for an on-site investigation; small areas of other soils sit inside every map unit.

usgs_geology_pr.name: USGS — Digital geologic map of Puerto Rico at 1:100,000 (Bawiec, 1998)
usgs_geology_pr.credit: Source: Bawiec, W.J., 1998, Geology, geochemistry, geophysics, mineral occurrences and mineral resource assessment for the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 98-38
usgs_geology_pr.access: The three 1:100,000 sheets of the main island, downloaded once by hand as ArcInfo export files into cache/geology/ (soils.py does not download them). Only the outlines of the young river, swamp and beach deposits (map units Qa, Qs and Qb) are used, to say what lies under land that the soil survey maps as Urban land alone; no geologic polygon is published.
usgs_geology_pr.used_for: The flooding answer of the Soils layer where the soil survey maps only Urban land: on young river, swamp or beach deposits, or not.
usgs_geology_pr.terms_note: USGS-authored data are in the public domain in the United States. The map is at 1:100,000: it tells the kind of ground under a neighbourhood, not under a lot. It does not cover Vieques or Culebra.

usfws_nwi.name: US Fish and Wildlife Service — National Wetlands Inventory

more_links.label: Data source service (photo year of each mapping project)

usfws_nwi.credit: Source: US Fish and Wildlife Service, National Wetlands Inventory, Puerto Rico (wetlands mapped almost entirely from aerial photographs of 1983), read October 2026
usfws_nwi.access: The inventory's map service (no key); the official zip download refuses scripts. The build keeps each wetland polygon's code, type and outline, splits it among the municipal boundaries and publishes areas only.
usfws_nwi.cadence: The inventory is updated area by area. The coasts, which hold almost all of Puerto Rico's wetland area, were mapped from photographs of 1983 and have not been remapped; most of the interior has only the inventory's interim scalable product.
usfws_nwi.used_for: Wetland and mangrove area of each municipio and the wetland share of its land (environment_series.json: wetland_km2, wetland_pct, mangrove_km2).

usgs_comcat.name: USGS — ComCat earthquake catalogue
usgs_comcat.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program, with the Puerto Rico Seismic Network
usgs_comcat.credit: Source: US Geological Survey, ComCat earthquake catalogue, magnitude 2.5 or more around Puerto Rico, 2000-2025
usgs_comcat.access: The event web service (no key), one request a year, magnitude 2.5 or more in a box around Puerto Rico. The build keeps each event's epicenter and magnitude in the local cache and publishes counts only.
usgs_comcat.cadence: Live. The observatory counts whole years and renews the last two when FPR rebuilds the data.
usgs_comcat.used_for: Earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more, and 4.0 or more, placed in each municipio every year (hazard_series.json: quakes_*).

bts_t100.name: BTS — T-100 Segment Summary by Origin Airport
bts_t100.credit: Source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics, T-100 Segment Summary by Origin Airport, Puerto Rico airports 2014-2025
bts_t100.access: The data.bts.gov API (no key), summed by airport and year. The build keeps the airport code, year, months reported, passengers and departures.
bts_t100.cadence: BTS adds a month about three months after it ends. A year is published once San Juan has all twelve months (python gateway_series.py).
bts_t100.used_for: Air passengers boarding and commercial flights departing in each municipality, every year (gateway_series.json: air_passengers, air_departures).

faa_enplanements.name: FAA — Commercial Service Airports, passenger boardings (enplanements)
faa_enplanements.credit: Source: US Federal Aviation Administration, Commercial Service Airports enplanements, calendar years 2023-2025
faa_enplanements.access: One Excel file a calendar year (no key), arp-cy{year}-commercial-service-enplanements.xlsx, which also holds the year before. The build keeps the airport code and the enplanements of Puerto Rico's rows.
faa_enplanements.cadence: FAA publishes a calendar year's final figures in the autumn of the next year.
faa_enplanements.used_for: Air passengers boarding in each municipality, FAA's count (gateway_series.json: air_enplanements_faa).

bts_ncfo.name: BTS — National Census of Ferry Operators
bts_ncfo.credit: Source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics, National Census of Ferry Operators 2020, 2022 and 2024
bts_ncfo.access: The operator segment, segment and terminal files of each census on data.bts.gov (no key). gateway_series.py keeps the terminal ids and points (to place each terminal in a municipality) and each segment's first terminal, passengers and trips; transport_inventories.py keeps, for the newest census, both terminals of each segment, passengers, vehicles, trips and minutes, and draws each crossing with the line of the NTAD ferry routes service (services.arcgis.com, NTAD_Ferry_Routes), which holds the 2020 census with the same terminal ids.
bts_ncfo.cadence: Every two years; the 2024 census was released in June 2026.
bts_ncfo.used_for: Ferry passengers boarding at the terminals of each municipality (gateway_series.json: ferry_passengers), and the Ferry routes and passengers map layer (ferry_routes.geojson).

more_links.label: NTAD Ferry Routes (the line of each crossing)

hud_public_housing.name: HUD — Public Housing Developments (eGIS open data)
hud_public_housing.publisher: US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Policy Development and Research (eGIS)

more_links.label: ArcGIS REST feature service (the build reads it)
HUD open data catalog (DCAT, states the licence)

hud_public_housing.licence: U.S. Public Domain (the licence HUD's open data catalog gives this dataset: the usa.gov public domain label); HUD adds a disclaimer of warranty and liability
hud_public_housing.credit: Source: US Department of Housing and Urban Development, Public Housing Developments (eGIS), Puerto Rico
hud_public_housing.access: ArcGIS REST query of the feature service (no key), STATE2KX = '72'. The build keeps the development code and name, total units, the scattered-site flag, the county and the geocoding accuracy code (LVL2KX), and the point. The housing authority's telephone, fax and e-mail, its executive director's, the address and the tenants' characteristics are not requested.
hud_public_housing.cadence: HUD updates the layer quarterly (date of coverage 06/2026 on 2026-10-17). The observatory re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python facilities.py --refresh hud).
hud_public_housing.used_for: Public housing developments on the 2D map (public_housing.geojson) and developments and units in each municipio (facility_series.json: ph_devs, ph_units).
hud_public_housing.terms_note: HUD says to map only addresses geocoded to the rooftop or the ZIP+4 centroid (LVL2KX R or 4); the others sit at the centre of a block group or tract. The observatory follows that: those developments are counted in their municipio but not drawn.

usgs_structures.name: USGS — The National Map, National Structures Dataset
usgs_structures.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS), National Geospatial Program

more_links.label: Structures map service (the build reads layer 51, Fire Stations/EMS Stations)

usgs_structures.credit: Source: US Geological Survey, The National Map, National Structures Dataset (fire and EMS stations)
usgs_structures.access: ArcGIS REST query of layer 51 (no key), state = 'PR'. The build keeps the identifier, name, feature code, state, load date and point; the address, city and ZIP code are not requested.
usgs_structures.cadence: USGS adds and edits structures continuously (the service said 'Data Refreshed October, 2026'; the newest Puerto Rico station was loaded on 2026-07-17). The observatory re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python facilities.py --refresh usgs).
usgs_structures.used_for: Fire and EMS stations on the 2D map (fire_stations.geojson) and their count in each municipio (facility_series.json: fire_stations). Also the road distance to the nearest fire or EMS station, by barrio and municipio (essentials_series.json, essentials_barrio.json).
usgs_structures.terms_note: Chosen over OpenStreetMap for fire stations on 2026-10-17: USGS has 94 Puerto Rico stations, OpenStreetMap 77, and 74 of those 77 lie within 500 m of a USGS station. For police stations USGS has only 8, so that layer uses OpenStreetMap.

usac_erate.name: USAC — E-Rate Supplemental Entity Information (open data)
usac_erate.publisher: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC), for the Federal Communications Commission's E-Rate program
usac_erate.credit: Source: Universal Service Administrative Company, E-Rate Supplemental Entity Information
usac_erate.access: Socrata API (no key), physical_state = 'PR' and entity_type = 'Library', asking only for the entity number and name, type, status, city, county, state, the public, main, bookmobile and kiosk flags and the point. Contacts, telephone, e-mail, web address and street address are never requested.
usac_erate.cadence: USAC updates the dataset daily (2026-10-16 on 2026-10-17). The observatory re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python facilities.py --refresh usac).
usac_erate.used_for: Public libraries on the 2D map (libraries.geojson) and their count in each municipio (facility_series.json: libraries). Also the road distance to the nearest library, by barrio and municipio (essentials_series.json, essentials_barrio.json).
usac_erate.terms_note: IMLS's Public Libraries Survey has no Puerto Rico rows, so USAC's list is the only machine-readable national source. In Puerto Rico it includes community technology centres and other community libraries registered as public libraries. Some of USAC's points fall in another town: those libraries are counted in the municipio of their address and not drawn. A few names carry a telephone number, which the build removes.

irs_eo_bmf.name: IRS — Exempt Organizations Business Master File Extract (EO BMF), Puerto Rico
irs_eo_bmf.publisher: Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Tax Exempt and Government Entities

more_links.label: The Puerto Rico file (CSV; the build reads it)

irs_eo_bmf.licence: US federal government work, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); neither the IRS page nor Treasury's data catalog states a licence; FPR confirmed this reading on 2026-10-17
irs_eo_bmf.credit: Source: Internal Revenue Service, Exempt Organizations Business Master File Extract, Puerto Rico
irs_eo_bmf.access: The Puerto Rico CSV (no key). The build keeps the city, the first five digits of the ZIP code, the subsection and the NTEE code of each organization; names, EINs, street addresses and financial fields are dropped as the file is read.
irs_eo_bmf.cadence: The IRS renews the file about monthly (the file of 2026-10-13 on 2026-10-17). The observatory re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python nonprofits.py --refresh).
irs_eo_bmf.used_for: Tax-exempt organizations in each municipio, in all, 501(c)(3) and by NTEE major group (nonprofit_series.json).
irs_eo_bmf.terms_note: The file lists organizations the IRS recognizes as tax-exempt, at their headquarters address. Many Puerto Rico nonprofits are registered only under Puerto Rico law and are not in it.

census_zcta_county.name: US Census Bureau — 2020 ZCTA to county relationship file

more_links.label: The national file (the build reads it)

census_zcta_county.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, 2020 ZCTA to county relationship file
census_zcta_county.access: The national pipe-delimited file (no key); the build keeps, for each Puerto Rico ZIP Code Tabulation Area, the municipio that holds most of its land.
census_zcta_county.used_for: Places a tax-exempt organization in a municipio by its ZIP code when its city is not a municipio's name (nonprofit_series.json).

wcrp_scm.name: Puerto Rico Department of Housing and Foundation for Puerto Rico — WCRP Social Capital Mapping tool, list of Comunidades Especiales
wcrp_scm.publisher: Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH) and Foundation for Puerto Rico, Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program
wcrp_scm.licence: No open license stated; an internal program file built jointly by PRDOH and FPR with CDBG-DR funds. FPR publishes it on the observatory with the program's approval (confirmed on 2026-10-19); others should ask PRDOH and FPR before re-using it

short.es: lista del Mapeo de Capital Social de WCRP

wcrp_scm.credit: Source: WCRP Social Capital Mapping tool (Puerto Rico Department of Housing and Foundation for Puerto Rico), list of Comunidades Especiales, date not stated (about 2019-2021)
wcrp_scm.access: The file COMUNIDADES ESPECIALES.csv of the WCRP Social Capital Mapping tool, in FPR's Community Resiliency Planning SharePoint site (folder Datos para mapeo), read on 2026-10-17. It lists 711 Comunidades Especiales by name, municipio and barrio with Yes/No flags for community assets. wcrp_social.py --import keeps only those three names, the polygon of comunidades.geojson each row matches and the nine asset flags, in wcrp_ce_assets.csv; the list's two hazard columns are left out. The list holds no personal data. The copy read through the connector lost the list's accented letters; wcrp_social.py restores them from the matching polygon's name where it can.
wcrp_scm.cadence: A one-time list: its date is not stated (the WCRP Social Capital Mapping list, about 2019-2021, from the Junta de Planificación inventory). No live source exists, so nothing refreshes it.
wcrp_scm.used_for: The community-asset flags of the Comunidades Especiales on the WCRP page (wcrp_social.json, assets): counts by municipio and each community's flags in its pop-up.
wcrp_scm.terms_note: Foundation for Puerto Rico runs WCRP in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH), with HUD CDBG-DR funds (U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development). The SCM manual calls the tool a joint effort of PRDOH and FPR. The list states no license or terms, so no open license is stated. FPR approved publication on 2026-10-19 and confirmed the same day that its approval covers republishing this list on the observatory. That approval is not an open license: anyone else who wants to re-use the list should ask PRDOH and FPR first. The WCRP page carries an 'In review' marker and may change.

epa_tri.name: EPA — Toxics Release Inventory (TRI), Basic Data Files
epa_tri.publisher: US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), TRI Program

more_links.label: Envirofacts download of the Puerto Rico file (the build reads it)

epa_tri.licence: EPA Standard Open Data License: unless otherwise specified, data EPA produces are in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); EPA disclaims any warranty
epa_tri.credit: Source: US EPA, Toxics Release Inventory, Basic Data File for Puerto Rico (reporting year 2024), downloaded October 2026
epa_tri.access: Envirofacts' download service (no key): the Basic Data File of Puerto Rico for the newest reporting year EPA has published (the build tries this year and the three before). One row per chemical; the build keeps one row per facility with its TRI id, name, industry sector, reporting year and point. Street addresses, parent companies and the rest are dropped as the file is read.
epa_tri.cadence: EPA publishes a reporting year's data the following summer and revises it later. The observatory re-reads it when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh tri).
epa_tri.used_for: TRI facilities in each barrio and municipio (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: epa_tri). Pounds of toxic chemicals released, in total and to the air, in each municipio (infrastructure_series.json: tri_release_lb, tri_air_lb). No name or point is published.
epa_tri.terms_note: EPA's data catalog (edg.epa.gov/data.json) lists its datasets under the EPA Standard Open Data License, which says EPA data are public domain unless otherwise specified; nothing on the TRI pages says otherwise.

epa_frs.name: EPA — Facility Registry Service (FRS), Facility Interests map service
epa_frs.publisher: US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Mission Support

more_links.label: FRS Facility Interests map service (the build reads layers 8 and 22)

epa_frs.licence: EPA Standard Open Data License: unless otherwise specified, data EPA produces are in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); EPA disclaims any warranty
epa_frs.credit: Source: US EPA, Facility Registry Service (Risk Management Plan facilities and Superfund National Priorities List sites), downloaded October 2026
epa_frs.access: ArcGIS REST queries (no key): layer 8 (all facility interests) for Puerto Rico's Risk Management Plan (RMP) interests, and layer 22 (SEMS_NPL) for Puerto Rico's National Priorities List sites. The build keeps the registry id, name, program, status and point; the address, city, ZIP code and web links are not requested.
epa_frs.cadence: FRS is updated continuously from EPA's program systems. The observatory re-reads it when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh frs).
epa_frs.used_for: RMP facilities FRS marks active and NPL sites currently on the final list, counted in each barrio and municipio (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: epa_rmp, epa_npl).
epa_frs.terms_note: EPA's data catalog lists every FRS layer under the EPA Standard Open Data License. FRS lists 157 RMP interests in Puerto Rico, 33 of them marked active; only the active ones are counted. Risk Management Plans themselves (and their offsite consequence analyses) are not read.

epa_attains.name: EPA — ATTAINS assessment units (water quality, Clean Water Act 303(d) list)
epa_attains.publisher: US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Water

more_links.label: ATTAINS Assessment feature service (EPA's hosted layer; the build reads layer 2, areas)

epa_attains.licence: EPA Standard Open Data License: unless otherwise specified, data EPA produces are in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); EPA disclaims any warranty; the layer's own licence text says EPA geospatial data are public domain unless otherwise specified
epa_attains.credit: Source: US EPA, ATTAINS, Puerto Rico assessment units (2024 reporting cycle), downloaded October 2026
epa_attains.access: ArcGIS REST query of EPA's hosted ATTAINS Assessment layer 2 (areas), state = 'PR' (no key). The build keeps the unit's id, name, category, impaired and 303(d) flags, reporting cycle and outline. Puerto Rico has no point or line units in the service.
epa_attains.cadence: States report every two years; EPA updates the service when it acts on a report. The observatory re-reads it when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh attains).
epa_attains.used_for: The share of each barrio's and municipio's area inside a unit on the 303(d) list (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: epa_303d_pct).
epa_attains.terms_note: Puerto Rico maps the assessment units of its rivers and streams as the land that drains to each assessed reach, so the 179 listed units cover about half of the island's land.

epa_greenbook.name: EPA — Green Book, non-attainment areas (lead 2008, sulfur dioxide 2010)
epa_greenbook.publisher: US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards

more_links.label: Non-attainment areas map service (the build reads layers 3 and 4)

epa_greenbook.licence: EPA Standard Open Data License: unless otherwise specified, data EPA produces are in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); EPA disclaims any warranty; the map service states 'Access constraints: None. Use constraints: None.'
epa_greenbook.credit: Source: US EPA, Green Book non-attainment areas (lead 2008 and sulfur dioxide 2010 standards), downloaded October 2026
epa_greenbook.access: ArcGIS REST queries (no key) of layers 3 (lead, 2008 standard) and 4 (sulfur dioxide 1-hour, 2010 standard), state_abbreviation = 'PR'. The build keeps each area's id, name, pollutant, current status and outline.
epa_greenbook.cadence: EPA updates the service weekly from its own database; designations change rarely. The observatory re-reads it when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh greenbook).
epa_greenbook.used_for: The share of each barrio's and municipio's area inside a lead or sulfur dioxide non-attainment area (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: epa_naa_lead_pct, epa_naa_so2_pct).

epa_lmop.name: EPA — Landfill Methane Outreach Program (LMOP), landfills with coordinates
epa_lmop.publisher: US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Landfill Methane Outreach Program

more_links.label: All Landfills in LMOP Database with Coordinates (EPA's hosted layer; the build reads it)

epa_lmop.licence: EPA Standard Open Data License: unless otherwise specified, data EPA produces are in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); EPA disclaims any warranty
epa_lmop.credit: Source: US EPA, Landfill Methane Outreach Program, landfills in the LMOP Database (data of September 2024), downloaded October 2026
epa_lmop.access: ArcGIS REST query of EPA's hosted layer (no key), county_state ending ', PR'. The build keeps each landfill's name, status, LMOP category, opening and closure years and point; the owner organization is not requested.
epa_lmop.cadence: EPA updates the LMOP Database about once a year (the layer was last edited on 2024-09-20). The observatory re-reads it when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh lmop).
epa_lmop.used_for: Municipal solid waste landfills, open or closed and still open, in each barrio and municipio (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: epa_landfills, epa_landfills_open).
epa_lmop.terms_note: EPA's data catalog lists 'All Landfills in LMOP Database with Coordinates' under the EPA Standard Open Data License. LMOP lists municipal solid waste landfills only: no open dumps, transfer stations, recycling centres, industrial or hazardous waste landfills. No source of open dumps or other solid waste facilities in Puerto Rico states terms (wanted.json: open-dumps).

hud_chas.name: HUD — Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data by census tract
hud_chas.publisher: US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Policy Development and Research (eGIS); tabulated by the US Census Bureau

more_links.label: CHAS by tract feature service (the build reads layer 1)
HUD open data catalog (DCAT, states the licence)
CHAS on HUD User (newer releases; refuses scripted downloads)

hud_chas.licence: U.S. Public Domain (the licence HUD's open data catalog gives this dataset: the usa.gov public domain label); HUD adds a disclaimer of warranty and liability
hud_chas.credit: Source: US Department of Housing and Urban Development, Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data, 2016-2020 ACS 5-year, census tracts (HUD eGIS), downloaded October 2026
hud_chas.access: ArcGIS REST query of HUD's eGIS layer (no key), STATE = '72': the tract id and three counts of Table 2 (all households; owners and renters with one or more of the four severe housing problems). The release (Date of Coverage) is read from the item's description.
hud_chas.cadence: HUD releases a new CHAS window about once a year on HUD User; the eGIS layer lags (2016-2020 on 2026-10-17, while HUD User has 2018-2022). The observatory re-reads the layer when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh chas), and the freshness check watches the layer for a new release.
hud_chas.used_for: Households with one or more severe housing problems and their share, by municipio (exact) and by barrio (an estimate spread from tracts by 2020 housing units) (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: chas_severe_hh, chas_severe_pct).
hud_chas.terms_note: HUD User's CHAS downloads (2018-2022, published December 2025) sit behind a bot check that refuses scripts, as its LIHTC, Fair Market Rent and Income Limits files do; the observatory does not get around it. The eGIS layer is the newest release a script may read. Counts in CHAS are rounded by the Census Bureau, and the layer publishes no margins of error.

census_tiger_lines.name: US Census Bureau — TIGER/Line Shapefiles, all lines (EDGES)

more_links.label: TIGER/Line 2026 EDGES files (the build reads the 78 Puerto Rico files)

census_tiger_lines.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, 2026 TIGER/Line Shapefiles, all lines (EDGES), Puerto Rico
census_tiger_lines.access: The 78 county files of the newest TIGER/Line year (no key; about 55 MB zipped), read with pyshp. The build keeps, for each road edge (ROADFLG = 'Y'), its id, feature class (MTFCC), its two topological nodes and their points.
census_tiger_lines.cadence: The Census Bureau publishes a TIGER/Line year each autumn. The observatory finds the newest year itself when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh tiger).
census_tiger_lines.used_for: Street intersections and their density per square mile, by barrio and municipio (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: street_intersections, street_intersection_density).

hhs_hospital_capacity.name: HHS — COVID-19 Reported Patient Impact and Hospital Capacity by Facility (geocoded hospital addresses)
hhs_hospital_capacity.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), healthdata.gov

more_links.label: Socrata API of the dataset (the build reads ccn and geocoded_hospital_address)

hhs_hospital_capacity.licence: Public Domain U.S. Government (as healthdata.gov states for the dataset)
hhs_hospital_capacity.credit: Source: US Department of Health and Human Services, COVID-19 Reported Patient Impact and Hospital Capacity by Facility (geocoded hospital addresses, last reported April 2024)
hhs_hospital_capacity.access: The dataset's Socrata API (no key): for Puerto Rico, each hospital's certification number and HHS's geocoded point, the last week it reported. Only the point is kept, in the local cache: it places the hospitals OpenStreetMap does not, it is where the build looks for the OpenStreetMap building of a hospital whose name matches only in part, and for the hospitals OpenStreetMap places by name it shows how far HHS's point lies from the building. Nothing from HHS is published.
hhs_hospital_capacity.cadence: HHS stopped updating the dataset on 2024-05-03, so it is never re-checked. Hospitals rarely move; a new hospital it lacks is located by OpenStreetMap or by hand (conditions.HAND_POINTS).
hhs_hospital_capacity.used_for: The point of 15 of the 52 general hospitals the drive time is measured to, and the place where the build finds the OpenStreetMap building of 8 more (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: hosp_drive_min, hosp_road_km). The points are cached locally and never published.
hhs_hospital_capacity.terms_note: HHS geocoded street addresses; for the 27 hospitals OpenStreetMap places by name, HHS's point lies a median 0.7 km and up to 5.6 km from the building, and in another barrio for 13 of them. That is why OpenStreetMap is tried first, and why which barrios show 0 minutes is uncertain near the 15 hospitals placed at HHS's point.

nps_nrhp.name: National Park Service — National Register of Historic Places, public locations
nps_nrhp.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Cultural Resources GIS, for the National Register of Historic Places

more_links.label: Map service (the build reads layers 0, points, and 1, polygons)

nps_nrhp.licence: Public domain: a US federal government work. NPS states no named licence; the map service's licence field says 'For general public distribution' and its metadata calls the public data general reference data. Treated as public domain, as other federal data are (decided by FPR on 2026-10-18)
nps_nrhp.credit: Source: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places, public spatial data
nps_nrhp.access: ArcGIS REST queries (no key) of layer 0 (points) and layer 1 (polygons), State = 'PUERTO RICO'. The build keeps the reference number, name, resource type, city, listing date, status and one point (for a listing with only a polygon, a point inside it); the street address is never requested.
nps_nrhp.cadence: NPS edits the data as properties are listed (Data.gov: updated 2026-09-18; the newest Puerto Rico edit was 2026-08-07 and the newest listing 2026-01). The observatory re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python community_assets.py --refresh nps).
nps_nrhp.used_for: Historic places on the 2D map (historic_places.geojson) and their count in each municipio (community_series.json: nrhp_places).
nps_nrhp.terms_note: Restricted and sensitive listings, such as archaeological sites, are not in the public data. NPS says the data are for general reference: using them does not satisfy consultation under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, and the points and outlines can be imprecise (most points come from the nomination's coordinates). NPS gives no warranty and asks users to get the data from its own servers. Private residences, and listings whose name holds a street address or house number, are counted in their municipio but not drawn, and their names are not published (decided by FPR on 2026-10-18; the reviewed list is nrhp_review.json in the repository). No address is published.

samhsa_nsumhss.name: SAMHSA — National Directories of substance use and mental health treatment facilities (N-SUMHSS)
samhsa_nsumhss.publisher: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality

more_links.label: 2025 National Directory of Drug and Alcohol Use Treatment Facilities (Excel and PDF)
2025 National Directory of Mental Health Treatment Facilities (Excel and PDF)
FindTreatment.gov (the live locator; not used, see the note)

samhsa_nsumhss.licence: Public domain: the directories carry SAMHSA's Public Domain Notice (they may be reproduced or copied without permission; citation is appreciated; they may not be reproduced or distributed for a fee without SAMHSA's written authorization)
samhsa_nsumhss.credit: Source: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, 2025 National Directories of Drug and Alcohol Use and of Mental Health Treatment Facilities (2024 National Substance Use and Mental Health Services Survey)
samhsa_nsumhss.access: The Excel file of each directory, found on SAMHSA's National Directories page (no key), read in memory. For each Puerto Rico row the build keeps the city, the state, the type-of-care codes (substance use, mental health, co-occurring) and a one-way hash of the name and address that joins the two directories; names, addresses, telephones and the files themselves are never written to disk.
samhsa_nsumhss.cadence: Yearly: the 2025 directories (survey of 2024) were released on 2026-03-06. The observatory looks for a newer edition on the National Directories page and re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python community_assets.py --refresh samhsa).
samhsa_nsumhss.used_for: Substance use and mental health treatment facilities in each municipio, in all and by type of care (community_series.json: bh_all, bh_su, bh_mh, bh_both). Counts only.
samhsa_nsumhss.terms_note: These are sensitive services, so the observatory publishes counts only: no facility name, address, telephone or point. The directories list the facilities that answered the survey and agreed to be listed; most individual practitioners are not in them. FindTreatment.gov, SAMHSA's live locator, is more current, but its API guide states no licence and speaks of 'approved users', so it is not used (wanted.json: samhsa-locator).

fpr_gii_2021.name: FPR — Global Innovation Index, Puerto Rico country profile (2021)
fpr_gii_2021.publisher: Centro de Innovación de Foundation for Puerto Rico

short.es: GII de FPR 2021

fpr_gii_2021.credit: Source: Centro de Innovación de Foundation for Puerto Rico, Global Innovation Index: Puerto Rico country profile (2021), calculated with the GII 2020 method of Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO
fpr_gii_2021.access: FPR's two-page profile (PDF created 2021-09-26) and its working file, both internal. The profile's 80 indicators, values, ranks and marks were copied as printed into docs/analysis/gii-2021/gii_original.json on 2026-10-23; the working file was read only to explain differences. No name, email or telephone number from either file is copied.
fpr_gii_2021.cadence: A frozen snapshot: the 2021 profile does not change. Corrections are notes beside the printed values, never edits.
fpr_gii_2021.used_for: The original values, ranks 'x / 132' and marks of the Global Innovation Index page of the Knowledge Area (gii_profile.json: value, shown, rank, star, hourglass, year).
fpr_gii_2021.terms_note: FPR's own calculation, not an official WIPO ranking: Puerto Rico is not in the official Global Innovation Index. FPR has not stated a license for the profile. Some 2021 values come from proprietary sources (IHS Markit country risk, Clarivate Web of Science, Brand Finance) and are shown as FPR published them, not updated.

wipo_gii2020.name: Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO — The Global Innovation Index 2020 (method and definitions)
wipo_gii2020.publisher: Cornell University, INSEAD and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)
wipo_gii2020.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO (report page ii); third-party data excluded

short.es: GII 2020

wipo_gii2020.credit: Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO (2020): The Global Innovation Index 2020: Who Will Finance Innovation? Ithaca, Fontainebleau and Geneva
wipo_gii2020.access: The report and its Appendix III, read for the framework (7 pillars, 21 sub-pillars, 80 indicators), the definitions (summarized in FPR's own words) and the marks of each indicator (composite, survey, half weight, higher is worse).
wipo_gii2020.used_for: The structure and the definitions of the Global Innovation Index page (gii_profile.json), and the method behind FPR's printed ranks. No other economy's GII 2020 data are published.
wipo_gii2020.terms_note: Licensed CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO: no derivatives without WIPO's permission. FPR's ranks place Puerto Rico's value among the GII 2020 values, so they derive from that edition; the page shows only Puerto Rico's values and the ranks FPR printed in 2021, and an open licence review records the question for Compliance.

wipo_gii2026.name: WIPO — Global Innovation Index 2026 database

short.es: GII 2026 de la OMPI

wipo_gii2026.credit: Source: WIPO (2026). Global Innovation Index 2026, database. Licensed CC BY 4.0. Adapted by Foundation for Puerto Rico; WIPO is not responsible for the adaptation.
wipo_gii2026.access: The database file (943,159 bytes as WIPO serves it, SHA-256 bbce0a2d...ffd73; a copy in a folder that SharePoint or OneDrive syncs gains customXml metadata parts and so another hash, which gii.py also records; downloaded on 2026-10-23 with FPR's approval) is kept in the local cache (cache/gii/2026/) and read with openpyxl in read-only mode by 'python -I gii.py --extract-2026', which keeps, for each of the 79 indicators, the screened values (no economy names), the year most economies use and FPR's checks of WIPO's method on its own data (direction, plain min-max or log transform, the range no winsorization caps, the rank rule). The extract stays in the cache.
wipo_gii2026.cadence: One edition a year (the 19th, 2026-09-29, 139 economies, 79 indicators). A new edition is read when FPR updates the page.
wipo_gii2026.used_for: The indicative GII 2026 position of Puerto Rico's updated value in 10 indicators whose source and definition match (gii_profile.json: c26_*): the number of economies with data, the year most use, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles and Puerto Rico's place among them, written X/N. Also the threshold of the change marker (chg_thr: 5% of the interquartile range of each indicator) and the structure, method and indicator list behind 'Changes in the index since 2020' (gii_changes.json).
wipo_gii2026.terms_note: CC BY 4.0 allows reuse and adaptation with credit to WIPO, the changes marked and a statement that WIPO is not liable. Third-party data in the database are excluded from WIPO's licence, so no economy's values are republished and no economy is named: only counts, the data year, three percentiles and Puerto Rico's indicative place. A percentile can coincide with one economy's value (the median in 8 of the 10 compared indicators), without saying which. Not an official GII rank.

wb_wgi.name: World Bank — Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI)

short.es: WGI del Banco Mundial

wb_wgi.credit: Source: World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators (2026 update), CC BY 4.0
wb_wgi.access: World Bank API, no key: api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PRI/indicator/{series}?source=3 for GOV_WGI_GE.EST (government effectiveness), GOV_WGI_RQ.EST (regulatory quality) and GOV_WGI_RL.EST (rule of law); read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/.
wb_wgi.cadence: Updated once a year (last updated 2026-09-25, data to 2025). Each release revises every past year.
wb_wgi.used_for: The updated values of indicators 1.1.2, 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 of the Global Innovation Index page (gii_profile.json: upd_value, upd_year), and Puerto Rico's 2024 values for their GII 2026 position.
wb_wgi.terms_note: Perception-based composite estimates with standard errors; the World Bank advises against reading small differences between years or economies as meaningful. Because each release revises the past, values from different releases are not comparable.

wb_wdi.name: World Bank — World Development Indicators (WDI)

short.es: WDI del Banco Mundial

wb_wdi.credit: Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, CC BY 4.0
wb_wdi.access: World Bank API, no key: api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PRI/indicator/{series} (the United States, USA, for the tariff), read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/.
wb_wdi.cadence: Updated several times a year (last updated 2026-10-08 for the series used).
wb_wdi.used_for: The updated values of indicators 3.2.3 (NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS), 6.2.2 (IC.BUS.NDNS.ZS) and 4.3.1 (TM.TAX.MRCH.WM.AR.ZS of the United States, FPR's method), the ICT components shown beside 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, and the mirror of UNESCO series used when it is newer (gii_profile.json).
wb_wdi.terms_note: Many WDI series for Puerto Rico are blank (logistics, domestic credit, market capitalization, patents, FDI, high-tech exports). The tariff of the United States stands for Puerto Rico because the US tariff schedule applies there; it is labelled as FPR's method.

unesco_uis.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) — Data API
unesco_uis.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO)

short.es: UIS de la UNESCO

unesco_uis.credit: Source: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS), UIS Data API, February 2026 release, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO
unesco_uis.access: UIS Data API, no key: api.uis.unesco.org/api/public/data/indicators?indicator={code}&geoUnit=PRI, read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/.
unesco_uis.cadence: Data releases about twice a year (February 2026 for the series used).
unesco_uis.used_for: The updated values of indicators 2.1.1 (XGDP.FSGOV), 2.1.3 (SLE.1T8), 2.1.5 (PTRHC.2T3.QUALIFIED), 2.2.1 (GER.5T8), 2.2.2 (FOSGP.5T8.F500600700) and 2.2.3 (MOR.5T8.40510) of the Global Innovation Index page (gii_profile.json).
unesco_uis.terms_note: Share-alike: an adaptation must carry the same licence. The series are revised between releases, so the printed 2021 values may differ from the current ones for the same year. Inbound mobility for Puerto Rico is a UIS estimate.

imf_weo.name: IMF — World Economic Outlook (DataMapper)
imf_weo.licence: IMF copyright and usage terms: free reuse with attribution

short.es: WEO del FMI

imf_weo.credit: Source: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook (October 2026), DataMapper
imf_weo.access: IMF DataMapper API, no key: imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/PPPGDP and NGDP_RPCH, read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/ (the server refuses this project's User-Agent, so that request goes with the library's default).
imf_weo.cadence: Twice a year (April and October); the latest years are IMF estimates and the following ones projections, which gii.py leaves out.
