imf_weo.used_for: The updated value of indicator 4.3.3 (GDP in PPP dollars) and the real GDP growth of the FPR estimate of 6.2.1 (gii_profile.json).
imf_weo.terms_note: The IMF allows reuse of its data with attribution, under its copyright and usage terms. Values are revised between editions: 2019 GDP in PPP dollars is 119.6 billion in the current edition, against the 126.9 billion FPR took from the October 2019 edition.

fac.name: Federal Audit Clearinghouse — single audits

more_links.label: Single audit rules (2 CFR 200, subpart F)

fac.licence: Public domain: "The data collected by the FAC is free to use and in the public domain" (FAC data page)

short.es: Federal Audit Clearinghouse

fac.credit: Source: Federal Audit Clearinghouse, US General Services Administration, single audits of the municipio governments
fac.access: FAC API (https://api.fac.gov), with a free api.data.gov key in the X-Api-Key header (FAC_API_KEY, HANDOFF decision 70; the only key the build uses, never stored in the repository or published). One request to the general table for every Puerto Rico audit (auditee_state PR, without the contact fields), then one request to the federal_awards table per fiscal year for the municipio governments' audits (first downloaded 2026-10-31).
fac.cadence: An audit is due 30 days after the auditor's report or nine months after the fiscal year ends, whichever is first, and many are late. The FAC holds audits of fiscal years 2016 onward; in the 2026-10 snapshot the observatory holds municipal fiscal years 2016 to 2025. It re-reads the list of audits only when FPR rebuilds the data (economy_series.py --fac --refresh), and downloads award lines only for fiscal years with new audits.
fac.used_for: Federal money spent by each municipio government in its fiscal year, in total, received directly or through a pass-through entity, and by federal agency (economy_series.json).
fac.terms_note: The FAC data page states that the data it collects are free to use and in the public domain (checked 2026-10-31). Audits of fiscal years 2016 to 2022 were migrated from the Census Bureau's clearinghouse to GSA in federal fiscal year 2024. The general table also holds the names, e-mail addresses and phone numbers of auditee and auditor contacts; the build never requests those fields.

lineage.en: Single audits filed by each municipio government: federal money spent in its fiscal year (July to June). The awards behind these dollars also appear in USAspending (as obligations, often to the Commonwealth) and in OpenFEMA; the stages differ, so they are never added together.

hud_lihtc.name: HUD — National Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Database
hud_lihtc.publisher: US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Policy Development and Research (HUD USER)

more_links.label: The database archive (LIHTCPUB.ZIP; saved by hand)
Missing data by year placed in service

hud_lihtc.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105: no copyright in the United States); HUD USER states no other licence for the database

short.es: Base de datos LIHTC de HUD

hud_lihtc.credit: Source: US Department of Housing and Urban Development, National Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Database, Puerto Rico
hud_lihtc.access: HUD USER answers scripts with a bot check, so the archive LIHTCPUB.ZIP is saved by hand from a browser to cache/facilities/lihtcpub.zip (HANDOFF decision 71) and the build reads LIHTCPUB.xlsx inside it. It keeps the Puerto Rico rows and these columns: the HUD project id, project name, city, state, latitude, longitude, 2020 tract and county, total and low-income units, year placed in service, construction type, credit type, the no-longer-monitored flag and the homeless and special-population targets. The street address and ZIP code are not kept.
hud_lihtc.cadence: HUD adds the projects placed in service in a year each spring (the release of 2026-05-28 covers 1987 to 2024; 2025 is due in spring 2027). Rebuilt with python facilities.py --only lihtc after a new archive is saved.
hud_lihtc.used_for: Tax credit housing projects on the 2D map and the 3D view (lihtc.geojson) and LIHTC projects, units and low-income units in each municipio (facility_series.json: lihtc_projects, lihtc_units, lihtc_li_units).
hud_lihtc.terms_note: The newer of HUD's two LIHTC sources: the eGIS layer of the same name stops at projects placed in service in 2020 (last edited 2024-12-09). HUD geocoded only some Puerto Rico projects to a point; the others carry a city only. Projects for people who are homeless or living with HIV are counted, never drawn or named.

nmtc.name: CDFI Fund — New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC) public data release
nmtc.publisher: US Department of the Treasury, Community Development Financial Institutions Fund (CDFI Fund)
nmtc.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105: no copyright in the United States); the CDFI Fund states no other licence for the file

short.es: Datos NMTC del CDFI Fund

nmtc.credit: Source: US Department of the Treasury, CDFI Fund, New Markets Tax Credit public data release
nmtc.access: The build reads the CDFI Fund's data releases page, takes the newest file named NMTC_Public_Data_Release_includes_…xlsx (the 2026-08-06 release: investments of 2001 to 2023) and reads its sheet of financial notes, one row per investment, with the project id, 2020 census tract, year, amount and state. No key.
nmtc.cadence: One release a year, in the summer, adding the investments of about three years earlier. python economy_series.py --nmtc --refresh looks for a newer file.
nmtc.used_for: Investment in low-income communities with New Markets Tax Credits by municipio and year (economy_series.json: nmtc_qlici, nmtc_projects).
nmtc.terms_note: The file also names each project's Community Development Entity and city; the observatory publishes only dollars and counts by municipio and year.

lineage.en: The CDFI Fund's public release of New Markets Tax Credit investments. Private investment made with a federal tax credit, not federal spending; kept out of spending totals.

usgs_water.name: USGS — Water Data API (reservoir water levels, river flow, groundwater levels and rainfall)
usgs_water.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS), Water Resources Mission Area; Caribbean-Florida Water Science Center

more_links.label: USGS, Hydrologic Conditions of Selected Reservoirs in Puerto Rico
USGS Real-Time Flood Impacts (flood reference points)

usgs_water.credit: Source: US Geological Survey, Water Data for the Nation (provisional data subject to revision)
usgs_water.access: OGC API, no key: monitoring-locations (state_code 72; site_type_code LK for lakes and reservoirs, ST for streams, GW for wells), latest-continuous (parameter 72376 for reservoir levels, 00060 for river discharge, 72019 for the depth to water in a well) and daily (72375; 00060 with statistic 00003, the mean of the day; 72019). Rainfall: latest-continuous by bounding box (parameter 00045, precipitation), daily with statistic 00006 (the sum of the day) and, from the page, continuous (the 15-minute readings of the last 24 hours, as CSV). The build reads the daily values; the page reads the latest values in the visitor's browser (the API allows requests from any site). Without a key USGS limits the requests an hour and answers 429 with the seconds to wait; river_gauges.py waits and asks again. Since 2026-11-12 the river build also reads the gauge height (00065) and, where reported, the water temperature (00010) of each river gauge, and the flood reference points of Puerto Rico from USGS Real-Time Flood Impacts (api.waterdata.usgs.gov/rtfi-api/referencepoints/state/46, no key).
usgs_water.cadence: Readings every 15 minutes or so; daily values the next day. The page reads the latest when a layer is switched on; the observatory rebuilds the daily values and usual levels and flows once a month (python reservoirs.py --refresh; python river_gauges.py --refresh; python groundwater.py --refresh; python rain_gauges.py --refresh).
usgs_water.used_for: Reservoir levels (reservoirs.geojson), River flow (river_gauges.geojson), Groundwater levels (groundwater.geojson) and Rainfall (rain_gauges.geojson) on the 2D map and the 3D view.
usgs_water.terms_note: USGS marks recent data provisional. Checked 2026-11-02: 121 lake or reservoir sites in Puerto Rico, 26 with a reading in the last 30 days. Checked 2026-11-11: 1,083 stream sites in Puerto Rico, 76 with a discharge reading in the last 30 days, 71 of them with at least 8 years of daily values in 2011-2025. Checked 2026-11-12: 5,197 well sites in Puerto Rico, 34 with a depth-to-water reading in the last 30 days; 83 sites with a precipitation reading, 54 of them in the last 30 days.

nasa_black_marble.name: NASA Black Marble — VNP46A3, monthly night-time lights (VIIRS on Suomi NPP, collection 2)
nasa_black_marble.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Black Marble team); distributed by NASA's Level-1 and Atmosphere Archive and Distribution System (LAADS DAAC)

more_links.label: Product page at LAADS DAAC (layers, quality flags, file format)
The method: Román et al. (2018), Remote Sensing of Environment 210, 113–143
The archive the build lists (for developers; downloads need a NASA Earthdata login)

nasa_black_marble.licence: NASA data from a NASA-led mission: Creative Commons Zero (CC0) unless a product is marked otherwise; NASA strongly urges users to cite the data
nasa_black_marble.credit: Source: NASA Black Marble, VNP46A3 collection 2 (https://doi.org/10.5067/VIIRS/VNP46A3.002), LAADS DAAC; Román, M.O., et al., 2018, NASA's Black Marble nighttime lights product suite, Remote Sensing of Environment 210, 113–143, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2018.03.017
nasa_black_marble.access: LAADS DAAC lists the files openly; a download needs a free NASA Earthdata login. The build reads one user token from the EARTHDATA_TOKEN environment variable (a GitHub Actions secret) and sends it only to LAADS; the site never calls NASA and visitors need no login (HANDOFF decision 75). One HDF5 file a month for tile h11v07, which holds all of Puerto Rico (about 70 MB); the build keeps a summary for each area and deletes the file. No image is published.
nasa_black_marble.cadence: NASA posts each month about seven weeks after it ends. The observatory reads the new months when FPR runs the build (python nightlights.py, or the Night-time lights workflow).
nasa_black_marble.used_for: The mean night-time radiance and the share of pixels of poor quality or gap-filled, by month (2012-01 to 2026-09) and by year (2012-2025), for the 78 municipios, the 901 barrios and Puerto Rico (nightlights_series.json, nightlights_barrio.json, nightlights_monthly.json). Also the months for night-time light to come back after Hurricanes María and Fiona, and the lowest month after each, by barrio and municipio (storm_recovery_series.json, storm_recovery_barrio.json).
nasa_black_marble.terms_note: NASA's data use guidance says data from NASA-led missions are CC0 unless marked otherwise, places no restriction on their use and strongly urges users to cite them; it also asks that NASA be acknowledged as the source and that use not suggest endorsement. The observatory will cite the product's DOI and Román et al. (2018) wherever the figures appear. The login is NASA's condition for downloading, not a licence term.

usgs_landsat_c2_st.name: USGS — Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature (ST_B10) and pixel quality (QA_PIXEL)
usgs_landsat_c2_st.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS) Earth Resources Observation and Science (EROS) Center, with NASA; copy served by Microsoft Planetary Computer

more_links.label: The copy the build reads: Planetary Computer, Landsat Collection 2 Level-2
USGS: Landsat Collection 2 surface temperature (method and accuracy)
USGS: Landsat Collection 2 quality assessment bands (QA_PIXEL bits)

usgs_landsat_c2_st.licence: US Government work, public domain; USGS asks that Landsat data be credited
usgs_landsat_c2_st.credit: Source: Landsat 8-9 OLI/TIRS Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature, courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey (https://doi.org/10.5066/P9OGBGM6), read from Microsoft Planetary Computer
usgs_landsat_c2_st.access: The build reads Microsoft Planetary Computer's copy with its anonymous access token (no account; the AWS copy is requester-pays), by HTTP range requests at the first overview (60 m), only the tiles over Puerto Rico (raster.py, about 2 MB a scene). The site never calls Planetary Computer. No image is published.
usgs_landsat_c2_st.cadence: A scene every 8 days on each of six path/rows with Landsat 8 and 9 together; the observatory uses the last three complete summers (June to September), so its figures change once a year, after September (refresh unit heat).
usgs_landsat_c2_st.used_for: The median and 90th-percentile land surface temperature on clear summer mornings, the share of land among Puerto Rico's hottest tenth and the residents living there, for the 78 municipios, the 901 barrios and Puerto Rico (heat_series.json, heat_barrio.json).
usgs_landsat_c2_st.terms_note: USGS-authored or produced data and information are in the public domain; USGS asks for credit ('courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey'). Planetary Computer's terms of use cover access to its copy, not the data's licence.

copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.name: Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance, Collection 1 — red (B04), near-infrared (B08) and scene classification (SCL)
copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.publisher: European Space Agency (ESA) for the European Union's Copernicus programme; copy served by Element 84's Earth Search on AWS (Registry of Open Data)

more_links.label: The copy the build reads: Earth Search, collection sentinel-2-c1-l2a (AWS Registry of Open Data)
ESA: Sentinel-2 processing and the Collection-1 processing baseline
USGS: how to read NDVI values

copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.licence: Copernicus Sentinel data terms: free, full and open use, with credit
copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.credit: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024-2026, processed by ESA; read from Earth Search on AWS (Element 84)
copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.access: The build reads Earth Search's public copy on AWS (no account, no key) by HTTP range requests at 40 m (the second overview of the 10 m bands, the first of the 20 m scene classification), only the tiles over Puerto Rico (raster.py), and keeps each scene's clear cells and their NDVI (about 1 MB a scene at most). The site never calls Earth Search. No image is published.
copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.cadence: A view every 2 to 5 days with Sentinel-2A, 2B and 2C; the observatory uses the last three complete summers (June to September), the window of surface heat, so its figures change once a year, after September (refresh unit vegetation).
copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.used_for: The median vegetation greenness (NDVI) on clear summer days, the share of land with dense vegetation and with little or none, and the residents living on land with little or no vegetation, for the 78 municipios, the 901 barrios and Puerto Rico (vegetation_series.json, vegetation_barrio.json).
copernicus_sentinel2_l2a.terms_note: The Copernicus Sentinel data terms allow free, full and open use, including reproduction, distribution, adaptation and commercial use, with the credit 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [year]' for modified data. Earth Search and the AWS Registry of Open Data serve the copy; their terms cover access, not the data's licence.

nasa_ecostress_lste.name: NASA ECOSTRESS — Tiled Land Surface Temperature and Emissivity, Instantaneous L2, 70 m, version 2 (ECO_L2T_LSTE.002)
nasa_ecostress_lste.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (ECOSTRESS science team: Hook, S. and Hulley, G.); distributed by the NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC (LP DAAC)

more_links.label: NASA Earthdata: the product's page (layers, quality flags, user guide)
NASA Earthdata: data use and citation guidance

nasa_ecostress_lste.licence: NASA Earth science data: no restrictions on use (CC0); NASA asks that the data be cited
nasa_ecostress_lste.credit: Hook, S., Hulley, G. (2022). ECOSTRESS Tiled Land Surface Temperature and Emissivity Instantaneous L2 Global 70 m V002. NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC. https://doi.org/10.5067/ECOSTRESS/ECO_L2T_LSTE.002
nasa_ecostress_lste.access: The build reads the LP DAAC's cloud copy with FPR's NASA Earthdata token (the one night lights uses, decisions 75 and 80), sent only to NASA's hosts; the LP DAAC answers with a short-lived signed address read by HTTP range requests, only where the barrios' cells fall. The build runs in GitHub Actions with the token as a secret. The site never calls NASA, and no image is published.
nasa_ecostress_lste.cadence: ECOSTRESS flies on the International Space Station and passes several times a week, at a different hour each time; the observatory uses the night passes (21:00 to 06:00) of the last three complete summers (June to September), the window of surface heat, so its figures change once a year, after September (refresh unit night_heat).
nasa_ecostress_lste.used_for: The median and 90th-percentile land surface temperature on clear summer nights, the share of land among Puerto Rico's warmest tenth at night and the residents living there, for the 78 municipios, the 901 barrios and Puerto Rico (night_heat_series.json, night_heat_barrio.json).
nasa_ecostress_lste.terms_note: NASA's data use guidance: data from NASA-led missions carry no restriction on use (CC0), and users are strongly urged to cite them. Downloading needs a free Earthdata login; the published summaries need none.

usgs_3dep_13.name: USGS — 3D Elevation Program (3DEP), 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) seamless digital elevation model
usgs_3dep_13.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS), National Geospatial Program

more_links.label: The files the build reads: The National Map's staged products on AWS
US Access Board: 2010 ADA Standards, 405.2 (the running slope of a ramp)

usgs_3dep_13.licence: US Government work, public domain; USGS asks for credit
usgs_3dep_13.credit: Source: USGS 3D Elevation Program, 1/3 arc-second seamless DEM, courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey
usgs_3dep_13.access: The build reads the newest version of each one-degree tile over Puerto Rico from The National Map's public files on AWS (no account), by HTTP range requests with raster.py: for climb.py only where the walks to the stops pass (heights every 10 m along the walks), for slope.py the whole of Puerto Rico in windows of 0.1 degree. The site never calls USGS. The published image is slope_surface.png, the mean slope of blocks of about 60 m; no image of heights is published.
usgs_3dep_13.cadence: USGS replaces a tile when better lidar arrives (the Puerto Rico tiles were last replaced on 2026-07-22); the climb figures are rebuilt with the nightly transit refresh, which only writes them when the walkers or the heights change.
usgs_3dep_13.used_for: The round-trip climb of the walk to a stop with a current timetable, and the residents whose walk has a stretch steeper than a ramp may be, for the 78 municipios, the 901 barrios and Puerto Rico (climb_series.json, climb_barrio.json); and the slope of the land: the share steeper than 15% and than 30% and the mean slope, by barrio and municipio (slope_series.json, slope_barrio.json), with the Slope layer's image (slope_surface.png).
usgs_3dep_13.terms_note: USGS-authored or produced data and information are in the public domain; USGS asks for credit ('courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey').

ogp.name: Oficina de Gerencia y Presupuesto (OGP) — budget data sheets (Sábana) of the Government of Puerto Rico
ogp.publisher: Oficina de Gerencia y Presupuesto, Gobierno de Puerto Rico
ogp.licence: Public documents of the Government of Puerto Rico; OGP states no licence for the data sheets

short.es: Sábanas de presupuesto de la OGP

ogp.credit: Source: Oficina de Gerencia y Presupuesto (OGP), Gobierno de Puerto Rico, budget data sheets (Sábana)
ogp.access: The build reads the links of www.presupuestos.pr.gov and its page for each budget, downloads every data sheet (XLSX) under docs.pr.gov/files/OGP/, and reads one line per agency, fund, program, concept and object of expense, in thousands of dollars. No key.
ogp.cadence: Twice a year: the governor's proposed budget in the spring and the approved budget at the end of June. python ogp_budget.py --refresh reads the site again.
ogp.used_for: The Commonwealth budget by agency, fund, function and concept of expense: spent, approved and proposed (spending_state.json).
ogp.terms_note: The sheets cover the agencies in the fiscal plan, not public corporations with their own budgets. A draft marked Privileged & Confidential that is posted on the site is not read.

lineage.en: OGP's own budget data sheets: the publisher of record for the Commonwealth budget. Federal funds in the budget (Fondos Federales) are also federal awards in USAspending (dedup group ogp_federal); the budget's figures are never added to USAspending's.

jp_pica.name: Junta de Planificación — Programa de Inversiones de Cuatro Años (PICA)
jp_pica.publisher: Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico
jp_pica.licence: Public document of the Government of Puerto Rico; the Planning Board states no licence

short.es: PICA de la Junta de Planificación

jp_pica.credit: Source: Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico, Programa de Inversiones de Cuatro Años (PICA)
jp_pica.access: The build finds the adopted program linked from jp.pr.gov, downloads the PDF and reads its agency tables with pdftotext (poppler): one line per project with its municipio, type and four fiscal years, in thousands of dollars. No key.
jp_pica.cadence: Once a year: the Board adopts a new four-year program after public hearings. python pica.py --refresh reads the home page again (needs pdftotext).
jp_pica.used_for: Recommended capital projects by municipio, agency and fiscal year (spending_pica.json).
jp_pica.terms_note: Project names are read but not published; only totals by municipio, agency and year. A draft for public hearing is not used.

lineage.en: The Planning Board's program of recommended capital improvements of agencies and public corporations: a plan, not appropriations or spending. Part of it is funded by federal money (FEMA, HUD, EPA revolving funds) that USAspending and OpenFEMA also report, and by the Commonwealth budget's capital lines (OGP), so its figures are never added to those sources.

eia_intl.name: EIA — International Energy Data (bulk file INTL.zip)

short.es: EIA de EE. UU.

eia_intl.credit: Source: US Energy Information Administration, International Energy Data (bulk file INTL.zip, October 2026), Puerto Rico
eia_intl.access: The bulk file INTL.zip (no key; 24,264,743 bytes on 2026-10-29, one JSON series per line) is downloaded by gii.py, which keeps only three Puerto Rico series in cache/gii/: INTL.2-12-PRI-BKWH.A (net electricity generation, billion kWh), INTL.44-2-PRI-QBTU.A (total energy consumption, quadrillion Btu) and INTL.4419-2-PRI-QBTU.A (consumption from nuclear, renewables and other).
eia_intl.cadence: EIA rebuilds the bulk files twice a day; the Puerto Rico series were last updated in February and March 2026, with data to 2024. gii.py reads the file again with --refresh.
eia_intl.used_for: The FPR estimates of indicator 3.2.1 (electricity output per million people, with the Census Bureau's population; gii_profile.json) and of IN.3.3.2 (low-carbon energy use, new in the GII 2026; gii_changes.json).
eia_intl.terms_note: EIA's copyright page says US government publications are in the public domain and asks for an acknowledgment of EIA as the source. The generation is net (it leaves out what the plants use themselves), while the GII 2026 takes gross production from the International Energy Agency. EIA counts wind, solar and hydro electricity at its energy content (3,412 Btu per kWh). FPR's use of these data is not endorsed by EIA.

bls_oews.name: BLS — Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS), state file

short.es: OEWS del BLS

bls_oews.credit: Source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025 state estimates (oesm25st.zip), Puerto Rico. BLS.gov cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from BLS.gov.
bls_oews.access: The state file oesmYYst.zip (no key; 7,563,829 bytes for May 2025, one .xlsx) is downloaded by gii.py with a descriptive User-Agent (plus the contact in FRESHNESS_CONTACT when it is set, as freshness.py does; bls.gov refuses anonymous requests) and read with the standard library. Only Puerto Rico's total employment (00-0000) and its 22 SOC major groups are kept, in cache/gii/.
bls_oews.cadence: Once a year: the May estimates appear the following spring (May 2025 in May 2026). gii.py takes the newest file with --refresh.
bls_oews.used_for: The FPR estimate of indicator 5.1.1 (knowledge-intensive employment: SOC major groups 11 to 29 as a share of all employment; gii_profile.json).
bls_oews.terms_note: OEWS counts wage and salary jobs in establishments and leaves out the self-employed, so it is not the labour force survey measure the GII 2026 takes from the ILO. Estimates are from three years of survey panels. BLS asks users to cite it as the source.

fpr_baseline.name: FPR — Eastern Region baseline (field survey and traced routes, 2025)
fpr_baseline.credit: Source: Foundation for Puerto Rico, Eastern Region baseline, 2025 (site visits and municipal routes traced in ArcGIS Pro)
fpr_baseline.access: FPR's internal Eastern Region baseline dashboard holds the survey of illegal dumping sites (21 records with coordinates). The municipal routes FPR traced for the baseline are in an ArcGIS Pro project, exported to fpr_rutas_municipales.geojson. The survey table was read from the dashboard on 2026-10-23 and copied into fpr_vertederos_clandestinos.csv. The source is internal; Finance and Compliance cleared publishing these two layers (2026-11-10).
fpr_baseline.cadence: Copied once, on 2026-10-23. FPR adds or updates rows in fpr_vertederos_clandestinos.csv, or exports the traced routes again, and runs fpr_baseline.py; which traced routes the observatory already has is worked out again at each run.
fpr_baseline.used_for: The Illegal dumping sites and Municipal routes mapped by FPR layers of the 2D map and the 3D view (illegal_dumping.geojson, fpr_routes.geojson).
fpr_baseline.terms_note: The dashboard's other topics are not republished. Its outage figures (SAIDI, SAIFI) come from the Energy Bureau, which receives them from LUMA every month (wanted.json, power-reliability). Of the 59 route stretches FPR traced, the 21 that the observatory's transit layers already cover are left out. The form records no date for each visit.

dtrh_cpi.name: DTRH — Índice de Precios al Consumidor de Puerto Rico (consumer price index)
dtrh_cpi.publisher: Departamento del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos de Puerto Rico (DTRH), Negociado de Estadísticas del Trabajo

more_links.label: The index on indicadores.pr (CSV from 1984, 2000-01 basket weights)

dtrh_cpi.licence: Government of Puerto Rico public information; the indicadores.pr copy is published under Creative Commons Attribution
dtrh_cpi.credit: Source: Departamento del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos de Puerto Rico, Negociado de Estadísticas del Trabajo, Índice de Precios al Consumidor para todas las familias en Puerto Rico (base diciembre 2006 = 100, revisión 2010).
dtrh_cpi.access: The workbook 'Serie Histórica Índice de Precios al Consumidor' (.xls, one sheet per year from 2007, all items and the 8 major groups), a plain download from mercadolaboral.pr.gov, no key; and the CKAN dataset on indicadores.pr (package_show API), whose CSV carries the index concatenated to 1984 and whose basket file carries the 2000-01 weights. inflation.py reads 1999 to 2006 from the CSV and 2007 on from the workbook.
dtrh_cpi.cadence: Monthly, about four weeks after the month (September 2026 was published on 26 October 2026). The indicadores.pr copy lags by several months.
dtrh_cpi.used_for: The Inflation page of the Knowledge Area (inflation.html): Puerto Rico's 12-month inflation since 2000, the 8 major groups, the budget calculator and income in constant dollars.
dtrh_cpi.terms_note: Published by the Government of Puerto Rico for public use; cite DTRH. April and May 2020 were imputed by DTRH (no field collection during the COVID-19 closure). The two DTRH files agreed in 230 of 231 shared months when checked on 2026-11-10.

frbc_inflation_expectations.name: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland — inflation expectations
frbc_inflation_expectations.licence: Free to use with citation of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland and the dataset DOI
frbc_inflation_expectations.credit: Source: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, Inflation Expectations (doi 10.26509/frbc-infexp).
frbc_inflation_expectations.access: The model's workbook, sheet 'Expected Inflation': expected CPI inflation over 1 to 30 years, monthly from January 1982, a plain download, no key.
frbc_inflation_expectations.cadence: Monthly, in the middle of the month.
frbc_inflation_expectations.used_for: The central path of the projection on the Inflation page and the US input of every method in its backtest.
frbc_inflation_expectations.terms_note: The model is re-estimated with all data each month, so its past values are close to, but not exactly, what was expected at the time.

frbp_spf.name: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia — Survey of Professional Forecasters, inflation forecasts
frbp_spf.licence: Free to use with citation of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia
frbp_spf.credit: Source: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Survey of Professional Forecasters.
frbp_spf.access: The workbook Inflation.xlsx: the median forecast of CPI inflation over the next year (INFCPI1YR) and the next ten years (INFCPI10YR), each quarter; a plain download, no key.
frbp_spf.used_for: A cross-check quoted beside the Cleveland Fed's expectations on the Inflation page.
frbp_spf.terms_note: Medians of the forecasters' answers; quarterly, so it can be up to three months older than the Cleveland Fed's figure.

acs1.name: US Census Bureau — American Community Survey 1-year
acs1.publisher: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey
acs1.licence: US Government work; cite the Census Bureau as the source
acs1.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year estimates, table B19013 (median household income in the past 12 months).
acs1.access: Public summary files on www2.census.gov, no key: per-sequence files under 1_year_seq_by_state (2010 to 2019) and table-based files acsdt1y{year}-b19013.dat (2021 on). Only the rows of Puerto Rico and the United States are read. 2020 had no standard 1-year release.
acs1.cadence: Yearly, in September, for the year before.
acs1.used_for: Median household income of Puerto Rico and the United States, in current and constant dollars, on the Inflation page.
acs1.terms_note: Survey estimates with margins of error at 90% confidence, published with each value. Income is in the dollars of the survey year.

usgs_wbd.access: watersheds.py reads the subwatersheds (HUC-12) and subbasins (HUC-8) of subregion 2101 (Puerto Rico) from The National Map's ArcGIS service (no key), outlines simplified by the service to about 20 m.
usgs_wbd.cadence: USGS updates the WBD a few times a year; the observatory reads it again when watersheds.py runs with its refresh option.
usgs_wbd.used_for: The Watersheds and streams layer: 227 subwatersheds (HUC-12) with their subbasin, area and 2020 residents (watersheds.geojson).

usgs_nhdplus_hr.terms_note: USGS-authored or produced data and information are in the public domain; USGS asks for credit ('courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey').

treasury_oz.name: US Treasury — Qualified Opportunity Zones: 2027 designations and eligible tracts (Office of Tax Policy, Data Transparency; CDFI Fund lists)
treasury_oz.publisher: US Department of the Treasury: Office of Tax Policy and Community Development Financial Institutions Fund (CDFI Fund)

more_links.label: CDFI Fund, Opportunity Zones: full list and map of designated zones (2027) and the 2018 list
Treasury and IRS announce the 2027 designations (press release, 2026-11-05)
IRS Revenue Procedure 2026-14: eligible tracts and how to nominate them

treasury_oz.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105: no copyright in the United States); Treasury and the CDFI Fund state no other licence for the files

treasury_oz.credit: Source: US Department of the Treasury, Qualified Opportunity Zones designated for 2027 (Office of Tax Policy, Data Transparency; CDFI Fund)
treasury_oz.access: The build reads Treasury's Data Transparency page, takes the newest files it names (OZ2-Designations-2027-Data-Transparency-<date>.xlsx: one row per designated tract with its rural status; OZ2-Eligible-Tracts-Data-Transparency-<date>.xlsx: every tract with the poverty rate, median family income and comparison-area income of the 2020-2024 ACS, eligibility and rural status), checks Puerto Rico's tracts against the CDFI Fund's full list of 2027 designations, and reads the CDFI Fund's 2018 list for the first round. No key.
treasury_oz.cadence: A round of designations every ten years (the next in 2036); Treasury can correct a file in between. python opportunity_zones.py --refresh reads the page again.
treasury_oz.used_for: The status of every 2020 census tract of Puerto Rico (designated rural or not, eligible, not eligible), the residents in zones by barrio and municipio, the first round's zones, and the map layer of the designated tracts (opportunity_zones.json, oz_tracts.geojson).
treasury_oz.terms_note: Treasury says its Data Transparency files may not be relied on to substantiate a tax return position: the IRS notices and revenue procedures are the official lists. The observatory publishes the figures as Treasury gives them and recommends nothing.

lineage.en: Treasury's own files of the 2027 designations and of the tracts eligible for them; a federal tax incentive for private investment, not federal spending.

census_commuting_flows.name: US Census Bureau — County-to-County Commuting Flows (American Community Survey 2016-2020)

more_links.label: Table 1 (residence county to workplace county), the file the build reads
Accuracy of the Data, multiyear ACS 2020 (margins of error)

short.es: Negociado del Censo, flujos de viaje al trabajo

census_commuting_flows.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, County-to-County Commuting Flows, American Community Survey 2016-2020 (5-year)
census_commuting_flows.access: One Excel file on www2.census.gov, no key (6 MB). transit_links.py keeps the rows whose residence is in Puerto Rico: one row per pair of residence municipio and workplace municipio, with the workers 16 and over and the 90 percent margin of error.
census_commuting_flows.cadence: Every five years (2006-2010, 2009-2013, 2011-2015, 2016-2020). The folder list of the Bureau's site is checked every 90 days; a new release needs a person, because the file's address and the texts that name the period change.
census_commuting_flows.used_for: The workers who travel between each pair of municipios, the share of each municipio's workers who work elsewhere, and where the simulated connections are drawn (transit_links.json, simulated_links.geojson; Knowledge Area page transit-links.html).
census_commuting_flows.terms_note: Survey estimates with margins of error: small flows are unreliable, and the page marks the pairs whose margin is as large as the estimate. The 2016-2020 period includes the start of the COVID-19 pandemic.

lineage.en: The Census Bureau's own tabulation of the American Community Survey's place-of-work question; the only open origin-destination data for Puerto Rico (LEHD LODES does not cover it).

iepr_publicos.name: Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico — Mapa de rutas de porteadores públicos (Autoridad de Carreteras y Transportación)

iepr_publicos.cadence: Published once, on 2020-03-19, and not updated since. The portal's record is checked every 90 days; a new file needs a person to look at it before it is published.
iepr_publicos.used_for: The map layer Público routes (2020 list), and whether a público route joined each pair of municipios (transit_links.json).
iepr_publicos.terms_note: The list has no timetable, fares, operators or dates: a route on it may no longer run and newer routes are missing. The observatory shows it as a record of 2020, never as current service. Credit both the Instituto and ACT.

lineage.en: The transport authority's own list of público routes, as the statistics institute published it; the only open list of público routes with their lines.

nhtsa_fars.name: NHTSA — Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS), Puerto Rico files
nhtsa_fars.publisher: US Department of Transportation, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), National Center for Statistics and Analysis

more_links.label: FARS downloads (one folder a year; Puerto Rico in its own subfolder)

short.es: FARS de la NHTSA

nhtsa_fars.credit: Source: US Department of Transportation, NHTSA, Fatality Analysis Reporting System, Puerto Rico files 2015-2024 (2024: Annual Report File)

nhtsa_fars.cadence: NHTSA publishes each year first as an Annual Report File (about 15 months after the year) and replaces it about a year later with the final file. The newest year's file is checked every 30 days; a change needs a person to look at it.
nhtsa_fars.used_for: Fatal crashes and the people killed in them by municipio and year (pedestrians and bicyclists, motorcyclists), deaths per 100,000 residents and per 100 million vehicle-km (crashes_series.json); the deaths along each simulated connection between municipios, published only as five-year totals (transit_links.json).
nhtsa_fars.terms_note: FARS records include each crash's place, date and time. The observatory publishes only counts by municipio and year and five-year totals along a simulated connection, never a crash: the exact place and time of a death can identify a person. The Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission keeps its own count, which can differ from FARS.

lineage.en: NHTSA's census of fatal crashes on public roads, coded by the Puerto Rico FARS analyst from police reports, death certificates and other records.
